title: vpc-kinetic-upgrade-controller-with-atomic-fallback-and-terraform-hooks
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Build and validate a VPC-focused runtime upgrade controller ("kinetic controller") that performs tenant-aware rolling upgrades of the data plane with zero customer-visible disruption and a deterministic atomic fallback path. This ticket covers the automation glue between Terraform/IaC, the runtime controller, preflight/health probes, and a tested rollback/playback mechanism.

Background: Private deployments must support predictable, auditable upgrades without service disruption or customer session loss. Current upgrade flows are partially manual and rely on ad-hoc scripts. We need a repeatable controller that can be triggered via IaC (Terraform apply), exposes safe checkpoints for compliance, and contains health-gated rollback semantics.

Goals:
- Implement the kinetic upgrade controller orchestration and Terraform hooks so upgrades can be initiated from the customer's IaC pipeline.
- Define and implement health-check quorum semantics (probe quorum) across control/worker planes.
- Ensure KV cache continuity for live slices during gradual replacement; reduce cold-start errors via transient warm handoff.
- Provide an "atomic fallback" path that can immediately rehearse and revert a tenant slice to the last-known-good runtime image with minimal token loss.
- Produce thorough runbook and automated audit records for compliance teams.

Design summary:
- Trigger model: Terraform runs a module resource (redwood_private_upgrade.trigger) that creates an UpgradePlan CR in the private control plane. The kinetic controller watches UpgradePlan resources, orchestrates the sequence and emits progress events back to Terraform/state via the module's outputs (status webhook).
- Sequencing: Controller performs per-slice orchestration in kinetic waves: Preflight -> Quiesce Connections -> Drain with windowed concurrency -> Replace runtime instance(s) -> Probe and observe -> Warm-handoff of KV prefixes -> Release traffic. Each wave has configurable concurrency and probe thresholds.
- Health gating: Implement probe quorum with three probe types: synthetic request latency/response-check, KV reconciliation check (cache hit-rate delta), and live-session continuity check (session token exchange). Each probe reports pass/fail and confidence score; the controller requires both an absolute pass threshold and relative improvement to proceed.
- Rollback/atomic fallback: If a wave fails to reach health thresholds within a configurable timeout, the controller triggers AtomicFallback: immediate redeploy of prior image on affected slice, reverse traffic routing, and a short-window compensating write suppression to avoid double-commits. The AtomicFallback is idempotent and emits a signed audit entry.
- IaC hooks: Terraform module exposes preupgrade_plan (read-only preview), upgrade_apply (creates UpgradePlan CR), and upgrade_finalize (mark plan completed). The module also supports an abort signal via a terraform resource that patches the UpgradePlan to state=ABORT.
- Observability: Controller reports granular events to Console (upgrade-events stream), traces upgrade phases, and surfaces token-level latency/cost deltas in the upgrade dashboard. Metrics: upgrade_phase_duration_seconds, probe_confidence, rollback_count, kv_cache_hit_delta_percent.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria array)

Security & compliance: KMS keys used to sign UpgradePlan changes; controller requires RBAC binding and audit logging enabled. Security review required due to Terraform-driven control-plane changes in VPC environments.

Risks: Partial probe coverage could misclassify failures; warm-handoff complexity for certain model sizes; Terraform drift if the upgrade controller fails between plan creation and completion. Mitigations listed in tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can create an UpgradePlan and receive status updates within the customer's VPC
Controller performs a staged upgrade of a test tenant slice with 0 dropped customer sessions under load test (99.9% rule)
Probe quorum logic prevents promotion when KV hit-rate drops more than 6% or synthetic latency regresses > 40% for >2 consecutive probe windows
AtomicFallback returns the slice to the previous runtime image within the configured rollback SLA (<120s) and emits an audit record
Runbook and automated audit logs exist and have been reviewed by Security and Compliance
End-to-end e2e test harness (Terraform -> controller -> validation) runs in CI and is green

Controller: implement wave sequencer, probe integrations, and AtomicFallback handler (owner: runtime-team)
Probes: implement synthetic requester, kv-reconciler probe, and session continuity probe (owner: reliability-team)
Observability: emit events/metrics and wire upgrade-events into Console dashboard (owner: observability)
Security: KMS signing, RBAC checks, and threat model review (owner: security)
E2E tests: create CI job that runs a dry-run + functional test using a sandbox VPC (owner: qa)
Runbook: draft operator-facing playbook and oncall checklist (owner: product ops)
Docs: add Terraform usage example and rollback troubleshooting guide (owner: docs)
Canary: run a canary on non-critical tenant slices then escalate to multi-tenant test cluster (owner: release-engineering)
